title: SCHEMA PROBE F - PawScript view switch in instruction block
description: Probe world: does an extra instruction block built from a PawScript expression pick up a player's tracked-item edit on the very next turn?
background: A featureless white room containing twelve numbered doors. Nothing happens here unless a trigger makes it happen.
instructions: This is a schema probe world. Keep every response to one short sentence. Do not invent events, characters, or scenery. Obey every extra instruction block exactly.
objective: Advance turns so the probe triggers fire.

possibleCharacters.name: Probe Subject
possibleCharacters.description: A plain figure in a grey coat who exists only so the world has a player character.

victoryCondition.condition: The player types the word VICTORY.

defeatCondition.condition: The player types the word DEFEAT.

trackedItems.name: View A
trackedItems.description: PROBE: static rule text for view A. Never changes.
trackedItems.initialValue: PROBE RULE A: End every outcome with the single capitalised word PINEAPPLE as its final word. Never mention walruses.

trackedItems.name: View B
trackedItems.description: PROBE: static rule text for view B. Never changes.
trackedItems.initialValue: PROBE RULE B: End every outcome with the single capitalised word WALRUS as its final word. Never mention pineapples.

trackedItems.name: View Mode
trackedItems.description: Either A or B. Only the player changes this, via the tracked-item editor.
trackedItems.updateInstructions: Never change this value. Only the player edits it.

designNotes: SCHEMA PROBE F. Three tracked items (View A / View B hidden and static, View Mode player-edited) and one extra instruction block whose content is a PawScript choose() over $view_mode. See probes/README.md in the infinite-worlds-architect repo.
